messages.body_plain:
I've finally managed to get back to this and have confirmed that rHadoop can work with gzip and bzip2 archives, but I have had some weird behaviour.

My normal DEL delimited data was not returning anything, so I decided to simply and tested with this data set:

apples,1
orange,2
grapes,3
apple,2
apple,1
orange,1

using the fruit names as keys and summing the numbers. A python test gives me my expected result:

apples 4
grapes 3
orange 3

When I run it through rhadoop on non-archived data I do not get the fruit names. Instead I get:

1 4
2 4
3 2

When I run it on either bzip2 or gzip archves the counts are right but I still have issues with the key names:

1 4
2 3
3 3

I've been beating my head against a wall trying to figure out what's causing these issues and any help would be very appreciated!

This is my script:

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript

require('rmr2');
require('rhdfs');

categoryCount = function (input, output) {

  mapreduce(
    input = input,
    output = output,
    input.format = make.input.format("csv", sep = ","),
    output.format = 'text',
    map = function(k, fields) {
      keyval(fields[[1]], fields[[2]])
    },
    reduce = function(key, vv) {
      keyval(key, sum(vv))
    }
  )
}

hdfs.init()

if ( hdfs.exists("/user/michael/ccCount") ) {

  hdfs.rmr("/user/michael/ccCount")
  print("Removed directory from previous run.")
}

categoryCount("/user/michael/fruit.csv", "/user/michael/ccCount/")

#categoryCount("/user/michael/fruit.csv.bz2", "/user/michael/ccCount/")

The test code appears to work.  I wrote the test case below without mapreduce.  My guess is that since glm() uses Y values of 0/1, we shouldn't expect the coefficients of the fitted model to match the coefficients of the test model which uses Y values of -1/1.  The gradient descent method used by the test code converges very slowly which is why I used a large number of iterations.

dims = 2
alpha = 0.05
test.size = 5

# x0 is bias column

testdata.df = data.frame(y = 2 * (eps > 0) - 1, x0 = 1, x1 = 1:test.size, x2 = 1:test.size + eps)

M = as.matrix(testdata.df)

Y = M[,1]
X = M[,-1]

plane = t(c(1, rep(0, dims)))

g = function(z) 1/(1 + exp(-z))

for (i in 1:1000000) {
    plane = plane + alpha * t(as.matrix(apply(Y * X * g(-Y * as.numeric(X %*% t(plane))), 2, sum))) }

cat("plane:\n")
print(plane)
cat("M:\n")
print(M)
cat("\n")

# Check results
for (i in 1:test.size) {
    # Calculate conditional probability
    p = g(apply(X[i,] %*% t(plane), 2, sum))
    cat("Y[", i, "]=", Y[i], " p(Y=1|X)=", p, " ",
        ifelse(Y[i] == 1,
            ifelse(abs(1 - p) < 0.01, "passed", "failed"),
   ifelse(p < 0.01, "passed", "failed")),

Hi
this is the most interesting line for me

201301291535_0013/attempt_201301291535_0013_m_000001_0/work/Rscript does not exist.

Rscript is part of an R installation. After a typical installation, it should be on the Unix shell PATH, that is it should be executable by just typing Rscript at the prompt. rmr expects that. You could run a streaming job like the following
hadoop jar <path-to-streaming-jar> -input <some-small-input> -mapper env -output <some-output>
or some such and inspect the output to find what the path variable is set to. Also a
type -a Rscript
on the node where the failure occured would be of help. Remember that hadoop jobs are run as a hadoop-specific user, not as "yourself" meaning your accout. The fact that Rscript is on the path when you ssh to a node is neither necessary nor sufficient.

Antonio

messages.subject_clean: Using R stored in a .jar in HDFS
messages.body_plain:
This can not be accomplished without patching the source. A complete proof of concept is in the now obsolete branch 0-install. The general plan is

At installation time
1) Compile R to a common location for all the nodes and to a common architecture (hardware, OS). This is because, despite assurances to the opposite by core members, R is not relocatable. If you compile it for installation to /tmp/R it's got to be in /tmp/R on every machine.
2) Package. I did tar, you did jar, not sure it makes a difference in this case
3) Move to hdfs

At job run time
1) specify the hdfs location with -archives option to mapreduce
2) in the mapper, before calling R, check that it is available. If not, find the tar in the current working directory, unpack and move to the installation directory (no, you can't use it where it is, Rscript breaks)
3) Call Rscript with the user specified script

You can do the first part by hand, no problem. For the second part, 2) and 3) require a patched source. In the current stable the mapper is a call to Rscript, if it's not installed it will fail. In the io-branch the mapper is a shell script that eventually calls Rscript after doing 2). I was discouraged from pursuing this approach further as it seemed hard to make work on a variety of platforms and it run afoul of common cluster IT policies (a.k.a. restrictions). The lack of feedback on the 0-install branch also didn't help.

Antonio
